newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Labour pledges to cut power plant emissions.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Labour pledges to cut power plant emissions.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party pledged on Monday to cut carbon emissions from power stations by 800,000 tonnes a year by 2010 if it wins the next election.

"We will double the Tory government's limited target for Combined Heat and Power (CHP) systems from 5,000 megawatts by the year 2000 to 10,000 megawatts by 2010," John Battle, Labour's shadow energy and industry minister, said in a statement. Labour says current CHP output is around 3,500 megawatts.
CHPs differ from conventional power plants by utilising the heat generated from producing electricity that is otherwise a by-product that literally goes up the chimmney.
Combined Heat and Power units are found in factories, offices and some community institutions, such as hospitals, rather than industrial power stations.

Combined Heat and Power plants can achieve thermal efficiency levels of 80 percent or more, compared with 34 percent for conventional coal-fired stations. Every 10 megawatt increase in CHP capacity will cut U.K. carbon emissions by 1,250 tonnes, says Labour.

Labour says it will give a strong bias to CHPs in assessing planning applications for new power stations and also allow some local authority capital to be released to enable investment in energy efficient measures such as community heating.

Battle said the current capacity of 3,500 megawatts represents only five percent of total electricity generating capacity in the U.K , poor compared with other European nations. Around 33 percent of Danish electricity was generated by CHPs.
A general election is due by next spring and Labour has long had a strong lead in the opinion polls.
